core_obligations: Injectivity (proof lines 15113-15120): for a specialization x -> x' there is a functorial map F_{x'} -> F_x compatible with sections, and since every point of X specialises to a point of Z the restriction map Gamma(X, F) -> Gamma(Z, F|_Z) is injective.

Reduce to the auxiliary sheaves (proof lines 15122-15140): write F as a filtered colimit of the auxiliary sheaves of Modules, note that restriction to Z is a left adjoint and that both section functors commute with filtered colimits, so one may assume F is of the auxiliary form.

Use the embedding (proof lines 15142-15158): for an embedding F subset G one has Gamma(X, F) = Gamma(Z, F|_Z) cap Gamma(X, G) inside Gamma(Z, G|_Z), by the stalk argument and the specialisation property; the embedding of F into a finite product of pushforwards of constant sheaves therefore reduces surjectivity to those sheaves.

Conclude with the connectedness input (proof lines 15159-15164): for a sheaf (Z_i -> X)_*underline S_i the section groups are Gamma(Z_i, S_i) and Gamma(Z cap Z_i, S_i), the hypotheses are inherited by Z_i, and the case of a finite constant sheaf is exactly the connectedness lemma for spectral spaces.
proof_roadmap: Show injectivity from the functorial specialisation maps.
Reduce to the auxiliary sheaves by filtered colimits and then to a finite product of pushforwards of constant sheaves by the embedding.
Inherit the hypotheses on the closed pieces and apply the connectedness decomposition for finite constant sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that sections of a sheaf on a spectral space agree with sections on a closed subset meeting every closure connectedly (statement lines 15098-15110). The proof (proof lines 15112-15164) shows injectivity by specialisation maps, reduces to the auxiliary sheaves through filtered colimits, further reduces to finite products of pushforwards of constant sheaves by an embedding, and finishes with the connectedness decomposition for spectral spaces. H2: a multi-step reduction, each step written out with its reason.
